subject: vintage radio broadcast
title: What If a Radio Show Made America Panic? The 1938 Panic Is Mostly a Myth

scenes.text: What if a radio play convinced America that Martians had landed? The 1938 headlines lied.
October 30, 1938. Orson Welles's CBS drama stages a Martian invasion of New Jersey as fake news bulletins.
Next morning the New York Daily News splashes panic across its front page. A legend of a million terrified listeners is born.
But a ratings service phoned 5,000 homes that night. Only 2 percent were listening. Most of America was tuned to a ventriloquist.
Six New York hospitals had no case linked to the show. No verified death. One lawsuit, dismissed.
Newspapers were losing advertising to radio, and used Welles to paint radio as dangerous. The panic was real. It was the press panicking.

description:
What if a radio drama convinced America that Martians had landed? On 30 October 1938 Orson Welles's CBS broadcast of War of the Worlds staged an invasion as fake news bulletins, and next morning the papers reported nationwide panic.
But the C.E. Hooper ratings survey that night found only 2 percent of 5,000 households listening, six New York hospitals had no related cases, no death was ever verified, and newspapers, losing advertising to radio, had every reason to exaggerate.
What should we run through next?
first_comment: The one million frightened figure came from a 1940 study that counted being excited by the show as panicking. Which famous panic should we run through next?
